extractions.description: The paper explores the use of Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) in Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) solvers to optimize branching decisions in the branch-and-bound algorithm through the "lookback" phenomenon. Two methods, target smoothing and a Parent-as-Target (PAT) Lookback regularizer, are proposed to incorporate this phenomenon into GNN training, leading to reduced B&B tree sizes and solving times. The study demonstrates significant improvements in solving MILP instances and discusses the implications for broader optimizations.

climate_change_is_central.quote: Branch and bound is the method of choice for solving a myriad of discrete optimization problems appearing in all sort of applications (a few named in the introduction of this paper) and it is the basic scheme of all commercial and open-source discrete optimization solvers. Thus, the impact of the research in the area is potentially very high, not only from a methodological perspective but also in terms of day to day challenges that we all face, including drug discoveries and climate change.
